analysis.investment_thesis: Landmark Global is a micro-cap immigration consultancy with ROE of just 0.21% — the low P/E of 5.25 is a value trap, not a bargain. There's no visible growth story, no institutional interest (FII 0%), and no moat to justify taking a flyer at a INR 52 Cr market cap.
key_strengths: High promoter holding of 72.44% signals skin in the game
Immigration consulting has secular tailwinds as Indians emigrate
key_risks: ROE of 0.21% is effectively zero — capital is not earning anything
Tiny INR 52 Cr market cap with near-zero institutional sponsorship (FII 0%, DII 3.37%)
Commoditized, low-barrier service business vulnerable to regulatory shifts (visa policy)
red_flags: ROE of 0.21% is a profitability crisis masquerading as a going concern
Low P/E with no growth = classic value trap — earnings likely inflated or non-recurring
Zero FII interest suggests no one with due diligence capacity sees a story here
analysis.detailed_analysis:
What's the story here? I can't find one. Landmark Global is an immigration consultancy — a business I can understand from the consumer side (Indians wanting to move to Canada, Australia, US) — and that sector does have a tailwind. But a 0.21% ROE tells me this company isn't capturing any of it. A P/E of 5.25 looks tempting until you realize that with ROE this low, the "E" is a rounding error; one bad quarter and the P/E triples. Without a growth rate I can't even compute a PEG, which is my bread and butter.

At INR 52 Cr market cap this is the kind of obscure small-cap where ten-baggers hide — but only if there's execution. Here I see none. No FII interest, minimal DII (3.37%), and a business model (visa consulting) that's notoriously fragmented with low switching costs and heavy dependence on destination-country immigration policy. I'd pass and watch for a turnaround story with real earnings traction before revisiting.
